steps.announcement: The 3 to insert is saved in base.
steps.explanation: Save the element to insert, 3 from the last index, 5, in base = 3. This prevents a later shift from overwriting and losing it. The array is still unchanged.
steps.key_state: The 3 is saved in base, and nums is still [1, 1, 2, 4, 5, 3].
steps.title: Save the final 3

steps.announcement: The 5 has been copied to index 5. The 3 remains in base.
steps.explanation: Compare the 5 at index 4 with base (3). Since 5 is greater, the assignment nums[5] = nums[4] copies 5 right to index 5. The array temporarily holds two 5s, while base preserves the original final 3.
steps.key_state: After copying 5 to index 5, nums = [1, 1, 2, 4, 5, 5]. Indices 4 and 5 both hold 5, and base is still 3.
steps.title: Copy 5 to index 5

steps.announcement: The 4 has been copied to index 4. The 3 remains in base.
steps.explanation: Continue left to the 4 at index 3. It too exceeds base (3), so the assignment nums[4] = nums[3] copies 4 right to index 4, overwriting the extra 5. The array temporarily holds two 4s, and base is still 3.
steps.key_state: After copying 4 to index 4, nums = [1, 1, 2, 4, 4, 5]. Indices 3 and 4 both hold 4, and base is still 3.
steps.title: Copy 4 to index 4

steps.announcement: The 3 has been written to index 3. The insertion is complete.
steps.explanation: Continue left to the 2 at index 2. Since 2 is no greater than base (3), stop shifting. The assignment nums[3] = base writes the saved 3 to index 3, replacing the extra 4 and completing this insertion. All six items are now in ascending order, and the two original 1s are unchanged.
steps.key_state: The 3 from base is now at index 3, giving nums = [1, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5]. This insertion is complete.
steps.title: Write 3 to index 3

prose.summary: Four steps show the temporary save, two rightward copies, and the final write. Each step's table gives the actual contents of nums at that point.
prose.title: Inserting one element: save, shift right, and write back

context: The input is nums = [1, 1, 2, 4, 5, 3] (indices 0 through 5). The first five elements [1, 1, 2, 4, 5] are sorted. Insert 3 at the correct position in the sorted range of nums: index 3, between 2 and 4.
description: Save the final 3 in base so that shifting right does not overwrite it. In turn, copy 5 and 4, both greater than 3, one place to the right. These assignments temporarily leave two 5s or two 4s in the array.

When you reach the 2 at index 2, stop shifting elements to the right and write the value saved in base to index 3. The top of the figure shows the original input for reference. Below it, four rows show the successive states of the array from top to bottom. The first of these rows still shows the initial array. The four rows in the table below follow the same order.

frames.explanation: Both right shifts are copy assignments. The value to insert, 3, stays in base until it is written to the position cleared for insertion.
frames.title: Inserting one element: save, shift right, and write back

summary: Save the final 3, copy 5 and 4 one place to the right in turn, then write 3 at index 3.
